_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A13, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a13/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
The reader located 212 of 315 designators on the board, 67 percent -- between
A18's good run and A17's poor one. A13's silkscreen mostly stands clear of the
component outlines, but the board is dense and a great many labels sit in
rotated columns two or three characters apart, which is where the collisions
come from.
Sixty-one designators the reader never returned at all are placed by hand from
a measuring grid over drawing_full.png. They are not a random sixty-one: almost
every one is a label drawn INSIDE its component outline (C24 in its box, U21 in
its DIP, L8 in the ferrite's square). tesseract segments connected components,
and an enclosing rectangle makes the label part of the graphics -- the same
failure as A17's touching labels, in a different shape. Read the tile around
C24 with any settings and it returns C19, L13 and R11 and never C24.
All ten test points are placed by hand too. The silkscreen convention for one
on this board is a rotated label with the pad drawn as a short bar beside it --
to the RIGHT
of the label for TP3, TP4, TP5, TP6 and TP8, and to the LEFT for TP1, TP7 and
TP9. TP2 and TP10 are the two horizontal labels, with the bar above the text
(TP2) or under it (TP10). Every box below spans label and pad together, so a
probe sent to the marker lands on the pad and not on the lettering.
Every marker on the board and on all three sheets has since been rendered and
looked at, one by one. The board came through clean: all 283, in every tier,
sit on their own label -- which is unusual, and worth recording, because the
tiers exist on the assumption that agreed is merely the best of four. The
sheets did not, and the three differ sharply:
sheet 1   83 of 115 right   agreed 70/80   ambiguous 10/21  single  3/14
sheet 2  107 of 133 right   agreed 93/105  ambiguous  6/16  single  8/12
sheet 3   23 of  78 right   agreed 20/33   ambiguous  3/30  single  0/18
Sheet 3 is the interconnect and decoding sheet and is nearly all text that is
not a designator; sheet 2 is dense circuit with few captions. That spread, not
the reader's settings, is what the per-sheet drop lists below reflect.

U23's pin-1 notch and MP4 across the whole of K4. R111 and R112 were read
onto R11 and R12. All four markers are removed rather than moved, because
there is nothing on this drawing for them to point at.

reader takes a row of it for the test point itself. The table's own zone
references settle which sheet each flag is really on: TP3 (PG1D2), TP4
(PG1D4), TP5 (PG1C7), TP6 (PG1A7) and TP8 (PG1A1) are drawn on sheet 1 and
keep their markers; TP1 (PG2C1), TP2 (PG2D2), TP7 (PG2B3), TP9 (PG2A8) and
TP10 (PG2D2) are on sheet 2, so their sheet 1 reads are legend rows and
nothing else. Dropped rather than nudged -- there is no net on sheet 1 for
Sheet 3 has no test point flag anywhere on it, and its TP1, TP2 and TP5 reads
are misreads of pin numbers in the diagnostic circuit and of the K1S/K1R
_dropSheet1Comment: Sheet 1 reads far better than sheet 3 -- 83 of its 115 markers were right,
and its agreed tier was 70 of 80. Every marker was rendered and looked at.
The 32 below were wrong and are dropped.
The AD7528's data bus is the densest source: DB1, DB2, DB3 and DB4 became
C81, C82, C83 and C84, and REFB became R71. Other pin and port labels: D7
as C7, D3 as Q9, '16 15' as Q10, '3' as H5 and as L3, '12' as L5, Y2/X1/Y3
as U6, -5S as U17, AGND/DGND as Z2, INHPH as Z1, INHPL as Z1's neighbour.
Captions and notes: 'QUADRATURE AMPLIFIER' as L15, 'SUMMING AMPLIFIER' as L2
and as H7, 'INTERGRATOR OUT ... CIRCUIT' as L7, 'SUMMING AMP IN' as MP2,
'QUADRATURE AMP IN' as U10, and the sheet's general note 'ALL RESISTORS ARE
5%, 1/4W' as VR4 and H4. MP4 landed on two rows of the test point legend.
Values and neighbours: '1N4448' as L8, '51K' as S1, R7's value as R2, C29 as
Q7, and L1 came out as a box the size of a quarter of the Z4/Z5 network --
which is also what check_data was reporting as Z4 and Z5 nested inside L11.
None of these designators is left worse off: C7, C8, L3, L5, L7, L8, L11,
L15, Q7, Q9, Q10, R71, S1, U10, U17, VR4, Z1 and the C8x run are all drawn
on sheet 2, and L1, L2, R2 and Z2 on sheet 3, where they are placed. U6 is
genuinely on sheet 1 and is placed by hand below. H4, H5, H7, MP1, MP2 and
MP4 are hardware with no symbol on any sheet.

93 of 105. Every marker was rendered and looked at; the 26 below were wrong.
Pin and port labels again: A2 as R2, A7 as R7, D4/D5 as C4, D3/D4 as U3, the
Y2 output pin '2' as L2, a Q-bar pin as U5, and pin 5A of P511 as S1.
Captions: 'DAC GAIN CONTROL' as L1, 'MULTIPLIER' as R1, '2VR & 22VR OUTPUT'
as K1, '2VR OUTPUT AMPLIFIER' as U7, 'QUAD AMP IN (PG1C6)' as U10,
'OSCILLATOR AMP IN' as MP1, 'PHASE LOCK CIRCUIT' as MP4, and the drawing's
Neighbours and values: U15's own label as C2, CR20 as CR22, CR17 as Q9, C78
R62's '10K' as Z5, '27pF' as H6, a SCOM triangle as VR7, 2N3906 as Z2, and
'A13-1 U30' -- the sub-assembly's own reference, not a part in the list -- as
S1, Q9, U10 and C75 are genuinely on this sheet and are placed by hand rather
than left dropped. The rest are placed correctly on another sheet, except
H6, MP1 and MP4, which are hardware with no symbol anywhere.
_dropSheet3Comment: Sheet 3 is the interconnect, decoding and diagnostic sheet: almost all of it
is text that is not a designator, and the reader cannot tell the difference.
Every marker on it was looked at. 23 of 78 were right; the 55 below were not,
and they fail in the four ways the sheet offers.
The pinout legend across the top right is the worst of them and it arrives
looking trustworthy -- Q6, Q7, Q8, Q11, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16 and CR13 are
captions of bottom-view outlines, and eight of the nine came through in the
agreed tier. Those transistors and diodes are drawn on sheets 1 and 2; on
sheet 3 they exist only as a caption, so the designator is right and the
marker is not. C6 and R70 are the same block read as designators ('BOTTOM
VIEW', a pin circle).
Pin numbers and port labels account for most of the rest: C4 and U3 on the
5801's O4/O3 outputs, U8 on O8, C122 on 'O1 20', U5 on O4/O5, U7 and U6 on a
digit of a value, L11/L12/L14 on 14/17/18/12, R6 on 3/4, U11 on PA7, Q9 on
A2, L2 on '2 A0', L5 and R12 on the DAC STRB/SEL row, R7 on IO5, MP4 on INH,
Z1 on INHPL, MP8 on PLOCK RNG, C5 on CS*, H7 on 24A/24C, C8 on '-15 S'.
Net names and ground symbols: K1, K2, K3, K4 and R33 on the K1S/K2S/K3R/K4S
coil drive nets, R57 on a RST winding label, S1, VR4, VR7, L7, L8 and Z5 on
SCOM / LHCOM / RLH COM triangles.
Neighbour misreads: C25 on C125, R19 and R29 on R109, H5 on C107, MP1 on
C104, U10 on a port column, R1 on a cell of the relay position table, L1 on
blank paper between two coil boxes.
K1-K4, L1, L2 and Z2 are genuinely drawn on this sheet and are placed by hand
below rather than left dropped.
_schematicComment: Hand placements on the sheets, in pixels of .build/a13/sch<N>_full.png.
TP9 and TP10 are the two flags the reader never found on sheet 2; each box
spans the flag symbol and the label beside it, so the marker points at the
net and not at a caption. Checked against the signal name printed on the
net: TP10's flag sits on the OSC OUT HI line above R110, which is what the
sheet 1 legend calls ISOLATED OSC OUT HI, and TP9's sits on P LOCK HI out
of P512 pin 6A/6C, which the legend calls P LOCK INPUT.
A later pass closed the sheet gap for another 36 parts: 11 on sheet 1 and 25
on sheet 2, sheet 3 gaining none. Two thirds of them were sitting in the
reader's output the whole time as `collision` hits that build_coords.py
discards outright -- the read was on the right label and the tier was the
only thing wrong with it. Check that tier before assuming a part was never
found: on this board C21, C62, C70, R36, C58, C59, R50, R65, R68, R79 and
R95 were all correct reads thrown away, and C40/C49, C60/C68, R11/R111 and
R36/R96 were pairs where one name of the pair belonged to a part on the
other sheet and one did not exist at all.
C77, C78, C80, C81, C82 and C83 are the six rungs of the Z1 39K ladder off
U17's CD4052 outputs on sheet 2, drawn two to a row. The reader found none
of the eight caps in that block by itself and the vision model found only
C82; the rest came from reading the block whole once its geometry was clear.
Absent from every sheet, checked by searching all three and looking at crops:
the nine HS heat dissipators (no symbol, as on the drawing); C126, C127,
R111 and R112, which this revision of the artwork does not carry either --
their reads resolve to C106, C107, R110 and R59 -- and R5 and R22. Those two
are Rev 9 scan artefacts: review.txt reports each as sharing a stock number
with a row that did join (R5 with R107/R35/R36, R22 with R12/R13/R83), which
is the merged-designator failure the Rev 9 OCR produces. They are on no
sheet, on no part of the drawing, and are the two items check_data.js still
reports unplaced.

_sheetsComment: Zone grids, measured from the tick marks in each sheet's own zone band rather
than from the frame lines: the ticks are what a draughtsman reads a zone off,
and on sheets 1 and 3 the frame's left border is at or beyond x=0 in the scan
so it cannot be measured directly. Each frame is a least-squares fit through
the seven column ticks and the row separators, which is why sheet 3's x0 is
slightly negative: its scan is cropped about 55 px inside the frame.
_notOnDrawingComment: Twenty-eight parts with no silkscreen designator: four rivets, four screws,
nine heat dissipators, two ejectors, the heat sink retainer, the air duct, the
silicone tape, three transistor mount insulators and three spacers. None of
them is drawn on Figure 7-15, so counting them as unplaced would make the
coverage badge lie. They stay searchable in the parts list.
Four more for a different reason. C126, C127, R111 and R112 are in the 1996
Table 6-16 and in neither the Rev 9 table nor anywhere on Figure 7-15 -- the
whole drawing was swept tile by tile looking for them. They are later
additions that this revision of the artwork does not carry, so they have no
silkscreen here either. The caveat in a13.reference.json says so.
R5 and R22 are here for the opposite reason: they are not parts at all.
Both come from the Rev 9 scan alone, and review.txt reports each as sharing
a row with designators that did join -- R5 with R107/R35/R36 (stock 721571),
R22 with R12/R13/R83 (stock 721548). Reading those two rows off the Rev 9
107' at quantity 13 and 721548 is 'R 12, 13, 83' at quantity 3. Neither row
contains an R5 or an R22 -- both are the OCR splitting a two-digit number,
which is why no silkscreen and no schematic symbol exists for either.
_layersComment: Alignment of the photograph to board space. Fifteen landmark pairs, each
one a designator whose silkscreen is legible in both images: C21, C22 and
C37 across the top, C68 at the top right, C55 down the left, C69 and U17
on the right, C93, C49 and C103 through the middle, Q10, R88, C95 and
C120 along the bottom, C85 at the right-hand edge.
Nothing is covering this board in the photograph -- the oscillator air duct
(MP8) and both heat sink retainers are off -- so U3, U9, U6 and the A13A1
daughter card are all in view and the landmarks reach every edge. It is the
best-anchored of the three.
The src side is not eyeballed: it is the reviewed board coordinate of that
designator from data/a13.coords.json, so it is the same point the markers
are drawn from. The dst side was not eyeballed either -- the locator
drawing is the silkscreen artwork, and the photograph shows that same
silkscreen in yellow ink, so the drawing patch around each designator was
cross-correlated against the photograph and each pair is a local
registration rather than a click on a pixel grid.
Fit residuals are 1.9 to 5.2 px on a 3000 px-wide drawing. Checked by
warping the photograph into board space and drawing the locator artwork
over it: the three big electrolytics, the relays K1-K4, the 82C55, L15 and
both card-edge connectors sit on their outlines. Sampling the whole board
with the same correlation afterwards gives a median residual of 3.0 drawing
px over 36 patches.
Marked approximate. The shot is not perfectly overhead, and the drawing
does not print every designator where the board does -- R109 and C7-style
labels are moved inside the part outline for legibility -- so a landmark is
the drawing's position for that part, which is the position the marker
uses, not necessarily where the board's own text sits.
src is normalised in the drawing (3000 x 1654), dst in the photo
